A Claude Code plugin that automatically opens the things Claude produces for you to read or reuse in your editor (VS Code by default):

  • Documents — specs, plans and other Markdown Claude writes under docs/, plus README.md, open when written.
  • Snippets — SQL, command lines and similar copy/paste text. The pastey skill has Claude save them as snippets/NNNN-meaningful-name.<ext> in your project, which opens them with syntax highlighting and keeps a numbered history.

How it works

A PostToolUse hook on Write, Edit and MultiEdit runs scripts/pastey_open.py. It checks the written path against allow/deny globs and launches your editor. A newly created file always opens; a file edited later opens only if it has not been opened yet this session. Source code never opens unless you allow it.

Install

Requires uv and an editor CLI on PATH (code for VS Code). The opener needs Python 3.11+; if none is installed, uv downloads one the first time the hook runs, so that first write can be slow.

Pick one of the two ways below. Using both would register the hook twice.

Try it for one session (plugin)

claude --plugin-dir G:\claude\pastey

Install it yourself (no marketplace)

Clone the repo somewhere stable, then run its installer. It copies the skill to <claude-dir>/skills/pastey and merges the hook into <claude-dir>/settings.json, keeping everything already in that file. Re-running is safe, and the first run saves your original settings as settings.json.pastey.bak.

uv run install.py install                    # for you, in every project (~/.claude)
uv run install.py install --project C:\work\myproj   # for one project only
uv run install.py status
uv run install.py uninstall                  # removes only what it added

Restart Claude Code afterwards. The hook points at the cloned repo, so keep the clone where it is; if you move it, re-run install to update the path. To update pastey, pull the repo and re-run install (it refreshes the skill copy). If your settings.json is not valid JSON the installer stops and changes nothing.

Using pastey

Pick a permission mode where writes can happen. pastey reacts to files Claude writes, so the write has to go through first. pastey was verified in manual permission mode (you approve writes), and accept edits mode does the same without prompting. In an auto-mode session a write was blocked once before reaching the hook, because auto mode's safety classifier gave no verdict on it, so no file existed to open. That is Claude Code's check, not pastey's. If writes are blocked, switch modes (Shift+Tab) and ask again.

Documents open on their own. Ask for a spec, plan or other Markdown under docs/, or edit README.md, and it opens in your editor when written. You do nothing.

Snippets need a nudge only if Claude forgets. The pastey skill has Claude save SQL, commands and similar text as snippets/NNNN-name.<ext> when you ask for something to copy. If it just prints the text in chat, say "save that as a snippet" and it will. Snippets are real project files: they are kept, numbered, and may be committed, so never ask for secrets in them. Add snippets/ to .gitignore if you don't want them in git.

If nothing opens, check in this order:

  1. Is the editor CLI on PATH? Run code --version (or your editor's equivalent).
  2. Did the write happen at all? A blocked or declined write never reaches the hook.
  3. Does the path match the allow list, and not the deny list? See Configure below.
  4. Read %TEMP%\pastey\pastey.log. Start Claude with PASTEY_DEBUG=1 to also log each raw hook payload.

Configure

Layers, later wins: plugin defaults, then ~/.pastey.toml, then <project>/.pastey.toml. editor and editor_args override; allow and deny lists add to the defaults.

editor = "code"                # any editor CLI on PATH
editor_args = ["-r"]           # reuse the current window
allow = ["reports/**/*.html"]  # HTML is not opened by default
deny = ["docs/drafts/**"]

Globs are relative to the project root and support ** (any depth), * (within one folder) and ?. \ is read as / and a leading ./ is ignored; [abc] sets are not supported.

Defaults: allow docs/**/*.md, docs/superpowers/**, snippets/**, README.md; deny docs/site/**, docs/roadmap.md. Deny wins over allow.

Limitations

  • The editor CLI cannot report open tabs, so a tab you close mid-session stays closed until the next session (or until the file is created again).
  • On Windows, a file whose path contains & | < > ^ % " is not opened (the code.cmd launcher runs through cmd.exe, so such paths are refused and logged). The skill keeps snippet names to a-z, digits and hyphens. A project folder with & in its name never opens files for the same reason.
  • Only text that becomes a file is opened; the skill is how chat text gets there.

Failures are logged to %TEMP%\pastey\pastey.log and never interrupt Claude. Set PASTEY_DEBUG=1 to log each raw hook payload.
